key_insight: LLM-generated interactions can improve long-tail recommendation accuracy and coverage while constraining overall accuracy loss.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can tune augmentation by item-popularity group to better serve sparse-data items without sacrificing overall recommendation quality beyond a chosen tolerance.
method: Partition items into groups by interaction frequency.
Optimize group-specific LLM augmentation for NDCG@20 and coverage, subject to an overall NDCG@20 degradation limit.
Test combined group strategies and ablate LLM scale and contextual richness under token constraints.
evidence_signal: SASRec experiments report group-specific NDCG@20 gains exceeding 100% and 60% for extreme and regular long-tail items on an industrial dataset, and 40% and 25% on MovieLens-32M, with increased coverage and no significant overall degradation.
watch_item: Individually optimal group strategies are not simply additive, and richer augmentation context increases cost, requiring joint tuning and budget-aware validation.
paper_title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
